text:
Maya: quick heads-up — ran a batch-classifier sweep on the canary cluster this morning. saw a weird sawtooth in p95 latency for short prompts (~<40 tokens) when the KV cache warmed and we flipped kernels. attaching notes below.

Ravi: ugh, saw that earlier in the profiler too. is this the same kernel-handoff we rolled last week? :thinking_face:

Maya: yes, looks correlated with the kernel-selector heuristics that prefer the fused-attn kernel for small seq len but only after kv cache fill hits ~20% occupancy.

Jin: can you paste the perf slice? which metrics spike — decode rate or queueing?

Maya: main signal is queueing jitter + decode-rate variance. p50 steady, p95 jumps ~120ms for short prompts during bursts. decode tokens/sec dips then rebounds. snippet: 
```
metric: p95_latency_short_prompts = 340ms -> 460ms -> 330ms (oscillating)
decode_rate_short = 22 tok/s -> 9 tok/s -> 25 tok/s
kv_hit_rate = 0.12 -> 0.48 -> 0.15
```

Priya: that kv_hit bounce is suspicious. maybe our kv-prefetch budget gating is overaggressive and causes an admission spike when warm-first-requests hit?

Sofia: also check batching: if classifier moves requests between length-buckets mid-flight that can split batches and force kernel switch. our batching boundaries are currently [0-32,33-128,129+].

Ravi: idea: introduce hysteresis on bucket assignment for short prompts — hold assignment for the lifetime of the request (don't reassign on decode-rate changes). reduces churn.

Jin: +1. we should also try soft token-budget caps per-batch: target tokens-per-batch 2048 for short bucket (instead of absolute request count) to keep kernel path consistent.

Maya: logged an experiment: toggled `batch_token_target_short=2048` and `kernel_handoff_threshold=0.4` on canary. results: saw p95 drop from 460ms -> 310ms and decode-rate steadier. KV hit variance reduced.

Priya: nice. any regressions for medium/long buckets?

Maya: small throughput loss for midlen (2-3%) since we constrained batch size, but tail latency improved. tradeoff seems acceptable for customer SLOs.

Sofia: we should add a small classifier feature: expose `decode_rate_bucket` in request metadata so downstream observability can plot cross-bucket handoffs. currently it's opaque.

Ravi: Agreed. Also propose a probe that simulates 1k short bursts at different arrival patterns (poisson vs bursty) to stress the kv warming path. tag: @Priya can you run the sim?

Priya: will run this afternoon. expecting results in ~2h. I'll post raw traces.

Maya: action items:
- Priya: run burst sim + attach spans (ETA 2h)
- Jin: add hysteresis flag + soft token-target logic (small PR)
- Ravi: draft canary plan to flip `kernel_handoff_threshold` gradually
- Sofia: add decode_rate_bucket telemetry (observability ticket)

deploy-bot: canary config change queued: batch_token_target_short=2048, kernel_handoff_threshold=0.4 — running smoke tests.

Jin: thanks — I'll open the PR and add unit tests for bucket hysteresis.

Priya: posted sim results: https://internal.imgur/sims/1735567890 — initial run shows p95 improvement consistent with the canary. attaching flamegraphs.

Maya: perfect. if smoke passes and Priya's sims look good, let's schedule slow rollout across canaries tomorrow morning. cc @Sofia for telemetry follow-up. :thumbsup:

Sofia: noted. I'll wire up charts for handoff-rate and kv-hit correlation.

Ravi: one more note — add a regression guard in the rollout: if midlen throughput drops >5% for 10m, auto-rollback. we've seen cascades once before.

Maya: added to the rollout doc. thanks all.

Sofia: also, let's capture a short blurb for the eng-runbook explaining why we prefer token-targets over request-count for short-bucket stability. helps oncall.

Maya: on it.

Jin: PR created: https://git.internal/runtimes/merge/789 — includes hysteresis + token-target implementation. reviewers: @Ravi @Maya.

Ravi: reviewing now. looks small and safe.

Maya: closing the loop — remind to monitor `kv_hit_rate` and `kernel_handoff_rate` on rollout dashboard.

deploy-bot: canary smoke tests passed. scheduled gradual rollout to 10% traffic in 30m.
